blocks.text:
Today you'll explore some of the lesser-known sites of the Sacred Valley of the Incas.

The Sacred Valley is thought to be one of the areas where Inca civilisation took shape. Good farming conditions made it possible to feed the population and free some people from full-time work on the land. This is thought to have helped the Inca Empire, Tawantinsuyu, expand.

Your first stop is the archaeological site at Chinchero. From there you'll head to Maras, where salt is still harvested from the ancient salt pans. The white terraces stand out against the valley's green fields.

Next is Moray, where immense concentric terraces resemble an amphitheatre. They are thought to have been used for Inca agricultural experiments. Differences in elevation and temperature allowed the Incas to recreate about 20 microclimates and adapt different crops to local conditions.

Each stop shows you a different side of the Sacred Valley. Chinchero is known for its archaeological heritage, the white salt terraces shape the landscape at Maras, and the terraces at Moray form a series of immense circles descending into the ground. In one day you'll see settlements, traces of ancient farming techniques and the natural contours of the valley.
5 January – Sacred Valley – Machu Picchu – Cusco

At the scheduled time, you'll transfer to Ollanta railway station.

The luxury **Hiram Bingham (Belmond)** train departs at **10:53**. The carriages feature classic interiors with dining tables. The train follows the Urubamba River into the canyon. Lunch is included on board.

At **12:24**, you'll arrive at Aguas Calientes station. Walk to the bus stop for the shared ride up to the entrance to Machu Picchu. The winding road takes about 25 minutes each way, and you'll travel with other passengers from the train.

Your guide will meet you at the entrance for a private tour of Machu Picchu lasting about **2.5 hours**. You'll walk among the terraces, passageways and temples and see the Intihuatana sundial and other sacred sites within the complex.

At **16:00**, tea is scheduled at the restaurant of the **Belmond Sanctuary Lodge**, by the entrance to Machu Picchu.

Afterwards, take the shared bus back down to the village. The Hiram Bingham departs for Poroy station at **17:50**, with dinner included on board. You'll arrive at **21:16** and then transfer to Cusco, a drive of about 30 minutes.

You'll spend two nights in a **Junior Suite** at **Belmond Palacio Nazarenas**.

The Hiram Bingham journey takes up much of the day and is an experience in its own right. Meals are served in the carriages as the scenery along the Urubamba changes outside your window. After arriving, you'll switch to a bus for the winding ascent to the archaeological site. The day pairs your visit to Machu Picchu with a comfortable journey there and back, lunch and dinner on the train, and tea by the entrance to the complex.
